chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
From the Sunnah is taking off the left sock before the right, and wearing the right before the left.

key_terms.الْخُفِّ: The sock (leather or fabric covering the foot)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended order for putting on and removing socks according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific etiquette (adab) for wearing and removing socks (khuff), establishing a preferred order of right before left for donning and left before right for removal. In Shia scholarly tradition, this practice is viewed as a manifestation of following the Prophet’s Sunnah, reflecting the broader Islamic principle of prioritizing the right side in daily actions as a form of spiritual discipline and imitation of the Prophet.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘From the Sunnah is taking off the left sock before the right, and wearing the right before the left’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is of the noble tradition to take off al-Khuff (half-boot) first from the left foot before the right foot and wear it on the right foot before the left foot.”’
